had this video been released a couple years back, it would've definitely relit my passion towards Kingdom Hearts, fortunately enough, it wasn't needed, for I now truly love Kingdom Hearts, all the way through, start to finish. my story with Kingdom Hearts begins with Recreio, a subscription magazine from way back when, my parents used to buy me every release weekly, I have no idea how many I ended up having, but picture 3 cardboard boxes full to the brim with these 20-ish pages magazines. There I saw it, the manga version of Kingdom Hearts Chain of Memories specifically I believe to be released by Panini, something about that boy holding that key-sword(?) just endeared me, I wanted to find and buy that so much, but never did, eventually I forgot about it; Then one day, while messing with my GBA emulator at my phone, I found Kingdom Hearts Chain of Memories, it was a couple years past that initial connection to Kingdom Hearts, I remember getting so excited to try it, and giving it up shortly after. I tried a couple times but never got too far, if I did go past a world I'd be surprised honestly. From there, a lot of years go past, eventually I learned about these games on the PS2, never got around to find them where I lived to buy, but I was fortunate enough that KH was easy enough to emulate that even my terrible notebook could manage to run all 3 games at 60 fps all the time, someway and somehow, maybe divine intervention. And played I did, kinda sort of, I did get to the final world on both 1 and ReCoM, but never got around to actually beating it. 2 was different tho, I liked it way more, I did everything that I could, I got around to defeating all the bosses, I got around to do literally everything that I could've except gummi ship missions and actually finishing Jiminy's journal. Some other years later, and I got around to play BBS, beat that one, hated to do so, still don't like that game. Also got around to try Days and ReCoded, never beaten both at the time, but really enjoyed ReCoded, years later it would end up being one of my favorites from the franchise. Eventually I learned about DDD, and at the time, in some way or another I ended up playing a bit of every release of Kingdom Hearts, but I was not aware of their significance, the story connecting everything, it was literally just "the Kingdom Hearts for the platform I can emulate", it was just "The Kingdom Hearts for the DS", the one for the PSP, the GBA and the PS2 at the time. With DDD, a little bit older and more curious, I learned that people hated its story, and story was just never something that I took interest at the time for Kingdom Hearts. I wanted to actually buy a 3DS for that game, and Kid Icarus Uprising alone, never ended up getting a 3DS tho, would've only played and beaten DDD years later, like, around 2 years ago on a phone that's strong enough to emulate both. But me being unable to play it made me even more curious, I finally gotten around to learn everything I could about Kingdom Hearts. And so I did, and then I treated that like it was the most convoluted and intricate story of all time, it was a point of pride that I had to force through everyone's throat constantly, looking back I can't help but feel embarrassed. Years later, getting closer to the point of this comment, me about 16-17 years old (now 22), starting his edge phase, I started to dislike Kingdom Hearts, still would go after everything releasing but moreso out of an obligation, be the one who knows everything and also be the one who mocks about it. That's the point that my pride turned into shame, and then again turned into a self aware joke: "yes, I know everything about Kingdom Hearts, and its ridiculous, don't play it, don't consume it, it's trash". Looking back, I can't help but hate this moment of my life. Finally, about 3-4 years ago, KH3 was already out for a couple of years, and I had out of obligation to see everything from it, and so I did. I felt something here and there, even through all my angst I couldn't help myself, but still, a lot of angst. Then I saw that Union Cross was finally reaching its conclusion, having tried to play it in the past and just not enjoying it, although loving to collect the medals. I started picking up the pace, watching just the mandatory cutscenes at that point, following Everglow's videos up to date. And then we get to it, to that scene. Union Cross' trilogy is ultimately about betrayal. The union leaders betray one another, the unions betray one another, your friends don't tell you everything constantly, eventually even your chirity betrays you. But above all else, MoM betrays everyone. His plan born out of betrayal, born out of fear, out of absolute hatred. If you rewatch the movie, you can see how MoM's roles are completely and utterly stupid, given to the worst people possible and sharing bits of knowledge that serve for nothing but conflict, that's was the point, to end in conflict. Learning about that was extremely interesting. But the game was not over yet. We finally got to it, the final battle, and the final betrayal. Your player character, not his very first time speaking, but still impactful nonetheless. Betrays his friends, he betrays the OG darkness, but above all else, he betrays you. Not longer the player's avatar, He's the enemy now, and you have to control his friends to defeat him. But it was all a bluff. Watching that made me feel something, and everything that came before and after that scene. "It takes so much effort to build something, but only a moment to destroy it", not a verbatum of what Skuld said, I imagine, but its a phrase I keep with me to this day. Just all the revelations one after the other, the cutscenes in between with MoM truly explaining his plan for Luxu. Luxu the Traitor; After a long long time, I was hooked again. I loved Kingdom Hearts again. In whatever game I play, I always nickname the main male character Makoto (not because I particularly love Persona 3, I loved the 4 movies but I have no interest in playing the games at all, I still need to change my pfp to Phosphophylite to stop getting confused as a fan of Persona lol, I just really enjoy how the name sounds), the female Lyra, and if there's some pet/monster at his side, it's Orpheus or Harp. But if there's an extra spot, it always goes to Everglow. The name just became meaningful for me after watching that video, watching in a premier, WHICH I HATE TO DO, but not at that time. It's my way of thanking him. Then Damo357 dubs the entire game, and, yeah, I can't help myself but cry every single time that I rewatch those 7 hours of hand picked cutscenes. Damien is the player character's name, he did too much to not deserve it. But everglow is the reason I'm in love with Kingdom Hearts again, why I go back to watch those same moments from KH3 and bawl my eyes out. Thanks for being a third reason of why I love Kingdom Hearts.

Great video as usual Jared! I’m a bit less confident than you regarding Takashi Kiryu and his management. Of course, we can’t really comment yet since the reboot isn’t effective for the public yet, but we can still note the various decisions made, such as the cancellation of Missing Link (I don't know if we'll ever find out the truth or see a reboot of the project). At the same time as this cancellation, they announced FF14 on mobile, a Dragon Quest mobile game, and Dissidia Duelum Final Fantasy. These are clearly choices made under his direction that are clearly questionable. They can of course use these “games” as fillers while waiting for the "reboot phase" but in my opinion, this gives a very bad image of their franchise and their name, because we’re not getting out of the mentality of the bad AA games released previously. I hope the company will seriously reevaluate its approach; I’m a bit skeptical of white-collar workers because they always seem to find a way to take bad ideas from elsewhere and apply them to their own company without really understanding what the public expects (This is more important than the defenders of these companies would like to believe). Square Enix's entire reputation and image are at stake here. This is what the investment group addressed to the president, but they received no response from him, which led to the release of the 100-page document warning that, in the "short term vision of thing for us" since Kiriyu took office, the company has failed to effectively manage its ambitions regarding public silence and transparency. Kingdom Hearts deserves better, and they could have anticipated this problem with Disney a long time ago, but they didn't... The series could benefit from transmedia efforts to bridge the gap in anticipation with the X saga and bring everyone up to the same level of understanding of the story. The final Fantasy Retrospective: Planning Stage I need some help with a project of mine. I decided a while ago that I wanted to play every Final Fantasy game, and that has ballooned out into a project to experience the entire series in the context of its contemporaries. I’m playing every main line Final Fantasy game, all their direct sequels, select spinoffs, and a selection of games that either inspired Final Fantasy games or were inspired by them. I need some advice for this project though to help me do it right. Any help with any of these questions would be greatly appreciated. &nbsp; 1\. I think I have pretty good list of JRPG’s (listed at bottom) that are relevant to Final Fantasy history, but I need help improving it. There are a couple of western RPGs on it, namely Ultima and Wizardry, that were big inspirations on the first Final Fantasy game, but I know that there has been more cross-pollination between the genres and I’d love suggestions for that. I’m also pretty sure that action RPGs have had a significant influence on modern Final Fantasy, to the extent that the upcoming Final Fantasy XVI is just straight up an action RPG. But the exact lineage of those games is something I have little info on. My list is clearly light in the last decade or so in that regard, although I’ve got some good picks of games influenced by classic Final Fantasy. Any suggestions are appreciated. &nbsp; 2\. I need historical info on the history of the series. I’ve found a few articles, but any articles, videos, or books that could give me better context on the history of Square and Square-Enix and the people who made these games would be great. &nbsp; 3\. I’m trying to experience these games in as authentic a format as I can, given that I do not speak Japanese. So I am prioritizing original releases with original graphics over remasters or remakes. I am also prioritizing official translations where I can. This brings me to an issue though, which is that Final Fantasy II, III, and V did not receive an official English translation until they were remade years later. I would like to play those games in their original form with an official English translation, or something close to it. Any information on translation patches like that would be appreciated. **NOTE: I am not asking for ROMs or information about ROMs. Only patches.** &nbsp; 4\. One way I want to make this experience authentic to how these games were played when they came out is that I want to rely on period-appropriate supplemental materials for advice and walkthroughs. I would appreciate suggestions regarding strategy guides, magazines, and period websites along those lines. &nbsp; 5\. Two of the main Final Fantasy games are MMO’s. I have already played Final Fantasy XIV up to current content (6.38 at time of writing) so I’m pretty good there. However, I would also like some sort of experience in Final Fantasy XI without having to actually commit to another MMO. How do you even get into FFXI in 2023? What is a reasonable stopping point for it? I don’t want to put another 500 hours into this one game, I’d like some sort of representative experience in it without grinding through 20 years of content. &nbsp; 6\. The most difficult game on this list to play in some reasonable state is probably Final Fantasy XIII and it’s sequels. Originally for the PS3 and Xbox360, it is no longer possible to play these games on a modern Sony console, which is what I own. Because of the weird architecture the PS3 used the PS4 isn’t directly backwards comparable. You used to be able to play an officially emulated version streamed to the PS4 via the PS Now service, but Sony merged PS Now with PS Plus a couple of years ago and dropped the PS3 Final Fantasy’s from the service. You can play the games with backwards compatibility on an Xbox, but I’m not buying a current gen Xbox. I’m already going to buy a PS5, I’m not putting another $500 investment in this project. The games have PC ports, but Square-Enix being Square-Enix they apparently run like crap. The best idea I have for this one is to buy a refurbished PS3 in order to play the games, but I’m open to any better suggestions if someone has any. &nbsp; For reference, this is my tentative games list for this project in rough order of release. How do you decide what to play next? How do you all decide what jrpg to play next? This genre seems to be one of the few where console generation doesn't matter and all so many excellent games and stories on every console and generation. I'm interested in your decision process more than specific game recommendations. Short version: I have so many jrpgs I want to play. I have a Legion Go so now i can find more time to play games after work. I want to finish all the final fantasy games I never finished. I want to play other non final fantasy jrpgs like Xenogears. Clair Obscur 33 just came out and seems amazing. I can't decide what jrpg to play next. It seems sensible to finish older games first, especially ones I already own. But Clair Obscur 33 seems so good and would be nice to play something as it's released and not need to wait for dlc incase it's unfinished product. Long version: ( ramblings) Up until last year I hadn't played any jrpgs or many games for a good number of years. It took me over a year to finish FFXVI just because I couldn't find the time to play or have access to the TV. Then while studying for an exam for my work I decided to play YS 1 and 2 on TurboGrafx16 emulator on my mobile as it seemed like a game I could just pick up and play without feeling like I'm getting too into it and can just play in 5 minute intervals during breaks. It turned out to be way more fun then I expected and had a great soundtrack and charm with the voice acting and animated sequences too. That then got me to play FF3 nes since I played 1 and 2 gba version decade ago during uni, again using emulator. I ended up finding out about and buying the pixel remasters but never opened it. NES version surprised me with it's gameplay and music. But in the middle of that, it was nearing Christmas and got the remakes as gift. So since I didn't remember finishing FF7 in school, I decided to play OG FF7 instead. Was originally planning on it just being after study sessions for work, but ended up staying up during night to play it and finish it. But now had no interest in the remakes. After it was finished, I ended up finding out about handheld consoles and ended up with a really cheap used legion go. I moved the ff3 save from my laptop to the legion go and finished it this year. Now I thought I'd finish playing all the final fantasy games that I never finished and never played (4, 5,6, 7 DoC, 13,13-2, 13-3). To keep things interesting, maybe mix up generations and do 13, 4, 13-2, 5, 13-3, 6. But then I was reminded about Xenogears and how I never completed that but it was still one of my favourites from what I played. And then I remember Legend of Dragoon being a game I always wanted to play. And also all the other Mistwalker jrpgs like Lost Odyssey and Fantasian. Then also Kingdom Hearts I never finished and seems like it would be better to finish before I get older and potentially put off by it. And now Clair Obscur : Expedition 33 has been released. Usually I just buy games used if it's for pS4 or 5 as I can find them dirt cheap and don't need to play the latest games anymore, as I've learnt my lesson about buying games when they were in sale digitally but having a backlog I never played or finished. But this game seems to be doing so well and seems reasonably priced, even used. And I'll know I'll enjoy and would be great to play something during the period it's actually released. And it seems like there's no need for DLC like ff15 and 16 so won't be missing out if if playing now. But I feel like there's so many older games I should play first and clear before getting modern ones. Especially now I have Legion Go where I can chip away at games easier.

The plot of Kingdom Hearts is basically that of Star Wars, Naruto and Matrix fused into one. The Keyblade and the Kingdom Hearts represent lightsabers and the Force, the dichotomy between the light, represented by positive emotions like love and altruism, and the darkness, negative emotions like fear, anger, hatred and suffering. In a distant Golden Age, the Keybladers founded their own Jedi Order on a faraway world. Some members grew greedy and selfish, starting a fratricidal civil war over the control of Kingdom Hearts, cataclysm that destroyed their world and began an endless cycle of conflict between Light and Darkness. After the cataclysm, the Order rebuilt itself in a new headquarters, but the Darkness resurfaced, and the survivors relocated once more.The new Grand Master decided to indoctrinate the new Keyblade wielders from childhood to completely reject the Darkness, to prevent them from falling into it. However, the brightest light casts the darkest shadow. The new enemy, disguised as an ally, manipulated a young man who had been rejected as a Master into embracing the Darkness, convincing him that he would gain the power to protect what mattered.. His friend, a dutiful and composed young woman recently appointed Master, faced the fallen keyblader in a bitter battle, which she won, but still ended up forced into exile, powerless to stop the Darkness, with only her regrets for company. The villain, in his boundless arrogance, aspired to become a god with dominion over life and death, as well as time and space themselves. Kingdom Hearts, enraged by such blasphemy against nature, retaliated by creating a boy who would end the upstart's reign, whom ancient legends identified as a Chosen One who would open the door to the Light, restoring the balance lost centuries ago. Years later,this seemingly ordinary young man with no Jedi training or education was chosen by Destiny to wield the Keyblade and vanquish the evil his predecessors had failed to stop. His adventure began by saving a beautiful princess from the clutches of the fallen hero, then his friend, and finally the keybladers lost to the darkness. The hero managed to defeat evil through empathy, forgiveness, and self-sacrifice, symbolizing the birth of a new Order of Keyblade Bearers. The attachments and love that had led so many into darkness became the very things that saved them from it. Like Naruto there are three main trios (Wayfinder trio, clock tower trio, Destiny islands trio) / (Sanins, team Minato, team 7), in which the same pattern is repeated: The rival / love interest of the main hero falls into darkness (Terra, Axel, Riku) / (Orochimaru, Obito, Sasuke) and one of them dies / is unconscious (Jiraiya, Rin, Naruto) / (Ven, Xion, Sora) and somehow all these nine people are related to each other. The series begins with the protagonist's call to adventure, facing a villain who tries to possess his rival (Orochimaru / Ansem), while in the second part the heroes face an organization of misfits dressed in black who seek to remake the world (Akatsuki / Organization XIII). The plot revolves around the conflict between two ideologically antagonistic factions (Light/Darkness - Senju/Uchiha) that are two sides of the same coin. One believes that love is the key to achieving peace, the other believes that power born from hatred is the key. Both authors give increasingly insane plot twists at the end of the play, such as resurrecting dead villains, stuffing bullshit powers into the plot (Rinnegan Sharingan / time travel, Power of Waking) and by abusing the man behind the man trope in a ridiculous way. , to the point that we thought it would be the final boss (Madara / Xehanorth) ends up being the pawn of his supposed right hand working for someone else (Zetsu / Xigbar) (Kaguya / Master of Masters). Well, I think Kingdom Hearts 2 and then Recoded explain the franchise's similarities to The Matrix quite well. A boy discovers that the entire reality he believed in is false and is forced to leave the cave to attain knowledge. However, we can compare Agent Smith and his clones to Xehanort and his extensions—a program that malfunctioned and became a virus which began to spread, threatening to destroy the entire system. The programmers created an antivirus in the form of Sora, who essentially turned the virus's weapons against it to defeat it. Sadly, the antivirus was discarded once it had served its purpose, lest it malfunction and become a glitch that would mess up the system.

Kingdom Hearts and my journey with it throught the years... A rant! (No spoilers, so relax) Kingdom Hearts. Oh boy... I remember Kingdom Hearts. Really fun memories of it too. I had an entire journey with it. My youth was filled with love for this... Until it grew to be just pure hatred. I had every possible version of most of the games. Bought consoles because of this franchise. Spent thousands upon thousands of money's worth to be with the characters I loved so much, even though they had really big problems... I'd like to share my story with this franchise and my thoughs/feelings towards all of this, since they're releasing a new compilation, KH4 is coming (probably this century) and I saw a post where people asked about it. Oh, and KH fans, this will probably piss you off. But oh well. Let me start by saying that **this franchise is the most ridiculous cashgrab that SE ever put their hands on**. Not even Final Fantasy had it this dirty. And the fanbase just eat it up like they've been hungry for years... Welp, because they are, since SE blueballs the hell out of them with teasers among teasers, a couple of good/great games and absolute trash for many years... With the promise of a masterpiece... That may never come. Kingdom Hearts has an amazing premise and the story (up until BBS) was very touching and epic, dramatic and emotional. That's how I saw it growing up. And I even maintain that view for some of the titles. Then I grew tired of SE's greedy sheenanigans. Not to mention Nomura's bullshit. Practically every console had its Kingdom Hearts back in the day and it was a real blast to buy a console just to play the "Next Kingdom Hearts!". I could not wait for the new ideas that could emerge... But they just kept getting worse and worse. So, here we go in order. Buckle-up, because its going to be long... and wild. **Kingdom Hearts** \- An amazing gem. A little rough, but it was awesome for what is was. The ideas were new (at the time). They had everything to be perfect: Two completely different fantasy visions clashing together to tell a completely original story. And what a story it was. It was dramatic, touching, really cliché... but it worked! Gameplay-wise it was just on point. I knew a bunch of people who thought Final Fantasy looked and sounded amazing, but were put-off because of the turn-based gameplay. Kingdom Hearts was just what they've been asking for YEARS. The beauty, the music, the story of Final Fantasy, but with an action-focused gameplay to match. It was fantastic indeed. **Chain of Memories/Re**: It was an interesting idea to expand the franchise to portable consoles at the time. Simpler narrative that connected to the story and all. Cool for the time. Then came the remake on PS2... Which showed it flaws. Not only that, it cranked it up to eleven. The story was tedious. The gameplay was... Also tedious. It worked on the GBA, but here... It was just for the remade cutscenes. **Kingdom Hearts II** \- Basically when the series peaked. It's (almost) perfect in every way, with very few problems, but that does not invalid its merits. The perfect equilibrium between Final Fantasy and Disney vision story-wise. The atmosphere was just it. Things got more serious. It wasn't just a goofy "lets not meddle!" but then meddles anyway. It was more serious. More... Consequential. Things were at stake. Things got real. The drama was on point. The epicness was... Epic. The fantasy was amzing. And it had just the right amount of fan-service too. It was... Amazing. This was the Definitive Fantasy experience I was looking for at the time. This was just... it! It had its problems, of course, especially with that bullshit of japan-exclusive version that expanded the universe and all, but still, it was worth every minute. Not to mention that sick teaser of people with amazing armour and keyblades in epic battles. The keyblade wars? What? HOLY CRAP, I NEED THIS! But then... **358/2 Days**: Not Kingdom Hearts 3. The DS deserved its shot too, I guess. You wanted to know more about the Organization? Here is a (veeeeeeeeeeery) depressive and absolutely tedious/sleep-inducing story about it. Not only that, it didn't even tried anything different with the gameplay. It was KH2 gameplay adapted to the DS. It was clunky as fuck. Technology-wise, though? It was kinda impressive, not gonna lie. A fully 3D game of that caliber running on the DS was nothing short of a miracle... Or a very skilled team. Kudos to them, honestly. **Coded/RE**: Once again, Not Kingdom Hearts 3. I can't, for the life of me, undertand why this shit even exists. Its just bad all around. But, hey! It has a cool less-than-a-minute cutscene that leads to the (true) sequel, so its worth it, right? FUCKING NO! It story is just so tedious that, holy shit, it could've been an YouTube video or an OVA (that was popular at the time) to just tease the next game. Instead, they made this very definition of a cashgrab. And. Called. It. CANON. Fuck off. **Birth By Sleep**: ...Not Kingdom Harts 3, but this... actually gives me a mixed feeling. It was teased on KH2:FM (the JPN Special Edition) as some big moment in the franchise's lore. (Keyblade Wars) Possibly even KH3! (suspiscions at the time), but then... Came this PSP game. And don't get me wrong, this was... Surpringly delightful. It had amazing ideas on how to draw the portable's power and to work around its limitations. The gameplay is amazing for what it is. Especially for the time. The story is... not perfect, but is has its moments. It was just... Fun. Like, KH1 fun. It had promise. This was it! It was really going somewhere! The remaster/port just shows that this was made for a portable device, just like MGS Peace Walker had with its remaster (transpharing. :v). It fucking SHOWS. I would say to you, if you're planning to play it, to do it on the PSP, but this would be hard as fuck, but at least keep it in mind when you feel weird about the PS4 version. Moving on. And then again... a new era was upon us. **Dream Drop Distance (3D)**: Oh boy... Where to even start. This fucking title led to so much confusion. Was it Kingdom Hearts 3? FINALLY? Nope. Its 3D! (because 3DS). Just another build-up for the real 3! That letdown aside, it was visually impressive. Trully. And the tease to it, holy crap, it was fun to accompany it. But then the game launched and... It was a fucking mess. The story was so, so bad. It had its moments, not gonna lie. Answered some questions, but then it threw WAY TOO MANY MORE IN YOUR FACE! Time-travel shit? Because they could not work properlly on what they've built before? Really? Gameplay-wise it was fine. They've worked on the basis they've built with BBS. Really interesting, with some new mechanics and all... But FOR SOME FUCKING REASON, the focus on the mini-games was cranked up to eleven. It was a portable console game, so whats the problem, right? This was kinda their thing after all... But boy oh boy, things would just get worse after this. ***Kingdom Hearts χ***: I don't need to say it at this point, do I? Of course there was a gacha. To be fair, it was SE's attempt at gacha, so it had its merits. They know how to build an interesting game. They just (AWAYS) fuck up the monetization. Many people say it was a really cool gacha though, and having played Mobius FF, I honestly believe them. But I here I was getting really tired. I just accepted that I was not going to play it for many reasons (not having a good mobile at the time, not really being into gacha, that kind of thing). HOWEVER, what I cannot accept is the fact that this is SOMEHOW canon... Of course it is. SE knows how to rip the wallets of the KH fanbase. The ones that didn't leave already would do almost everything to get to that sooooooooo anticipated KH3. (I was one of them, so I know what I'm talking about... even though I didn't went with the hype for this one). Then came the announcement: "Hey, we are changing engines!" This would be an amazing oportunity for the franchise. What was shown was really cool! **χ Back Cover**: "Say, how can we expand on **χ**'s lore without making a wave o people hate us... More than they already do? You know... Because of the gacha thingy. Welp, let's launch a (sort of) movie and compile it with the remasters that covers the general concept of the gacha!" Honestly, it was quite pretty to see that art-style with modern visuals, but that story was so... convoluded and boring (not tedious, just meh), that I had to force myself to see it. It was canon after all. At least it was over quickly. Like needle-quick. Whatever. **2.8 Final Chapter Prologue**: A collection of remasters for the PS4 that included the promised \*teaser\* *Kingdom Hearts 0.2: Birth by Sleep – A Fragmentary Passage.* Finally the story about a returning character that we aways wanted to see! Even if it was just a teaser for KH3. It ran like shit on PS4. Frames were all over the place. Stuttered like hell. But hey, finally something new and that was half good. We got to see what happened to a long-forgotten loved character, new mechanics, the new vision for the gameplay that was perfected in KH2, reworked on BBS, worked upon on 3D for this new style. It was interesting. It was like... 2h of gameplay? But it was an "extra" included in the collection nonetheless, so it got its money's worth. This was it, guys! Finally, the moment had come! IT WAS TIME FOR THE GAME'S FINALLE! KH3 WAS UPON US! We survived. Endured. Spent thousands of moneys-worth in consoles and games that got relauched, remade, remastered, re-re-re-re... And, to be fair, I'm not against it. The exclusivity bullshit for the consoles really worked to its detriment. It was really good to compile everything to the current-at-the-time consoles and let it be more accessible. But finally, it was here. This was it. The culmination of EVERYTHING we've been through. Finally closure! And... AND... Came another annoucement: "Kingdom Hearts 3 won't be the franchise's end. It would only finish the Xehanorth saga. Sora' story would continue on!" ...Oh no... no-no-no-no-no-no-no-no-no... This should not come as a surprise to ANYONE. It printed money, for crying out loud. It was obvious they wouldn't let the bone go. But this... Got me panicking for what was to come... Oh boy. **Kingom Hearts III** \- (This time for reals) It was here. It was finally here. I could not believe it. I had bought consoles for this franchise. In hope that they would release the ending to the epic saga. With many ups and way too many downs, but here it was at last. I've been waiting for what? Almost *fifteen years*? But... Oh, crap... Fucking hell. This franchise... It just can't let the fans have it. For fuck sake, why? I know Nomura has his quirks. I know SE misses more than it lands, but, fuck me, why.. AND HOW they fucked this up so badly? This piece of crap is just the culmination of everything that could be wrong with a franchise. The story is an absolute mess, convoluted as fuck, filled to the bone with retcons (in a way that shit on the fans intelligence), fan-service that leads to fucking NOWHERE (after blueballing you to hell and back) and, not only that, it was incomplete for the first couple of years. After what felt an eternity of endless teases and build-up and all.. For this piece os shit. Gameplay-wise... It's also a mess. It has its moments, but in general is just a mini-game galore. The series was already known for featuring mini-games, but they were fun little extras. NOT PART OF THE CORE, FFS! It didn't expand on the mechanics that did the other games good. They just thought "Hey, woudn't this be cool? Lets add it to the game!". Its almost had no general direction. And that intro... It. Was. A. Mess. It just added more bullshit for spectacle. Which was really tiresome after a quick while. I cannot put it enought into words how much I hate this game. For many reasons. Technical issues. Its quality in general... Maybe even my own ingenuity and expectation... But this was just... Terrible. In the end I had finished the original games when they launched and then replayed the re-releases when they launched... And then played again in the build-up for 3. Playing again made me understand some things, like some more, hate other way more... But it was quite a journey. It was interesting. A couple of years later I decided to give it another change... then I played 3 again. After a couple of hours I could not stand the having some of the most ultrageous retcons I've ever seen thrown in my face like that. This was it for me. I really couldn't stand it. A few weeks after that my whole Kingdom Hearts collection was gone. I sold it for almost nothing. Out of pure spite. I'm not rich, I pretty much needed the money. I like to collect figures and games and all, but I just wanted to get rid of it. I was done with this franchise. But hey, if you want to try and experience for yourself, I really think you should. This is video game history and a pretty important part on it too. It has many ups and way too many downs, but the personal experience should count more in this case. Who knows? Maybe you'll love it even with its many problems. The Whole remastered collection (without the last DLC and the musical game, which I really didn't play because at this point I was way done) is not really cheap, but you can get your money's worth out of a bunch of games. A lot of them are pretty much filler, though, so keep that in mind. Thats it. Thanks for reading this rant! =)

Nomura's new interview talks about his vision for FF7R, which is to "correct and unify the distortions in perception" (translation included) I used ChatGPT to translate the first section in this interview, which is about FF7R. The rest is about og FF7's creation and KH4. **Q: This year saw the release of "FINAL FANTASY VII REBIRTH" ("Rebirth"), the long-awaited second installment in the "FINAL FANTASY VII" ("FF7") remake project trilogy. What goals did you hope to achieve with this work?** A: The goal of the remake trilogy, rather than being a "remaster," is driven by the desire to "correct and unify the distortions in perception." Typically, a remake is about keeping the game system and story the same while simply improving the graphics. However, in this case, more than twenty years have passed since the original, and merely enhancing the graphics wouldn't align with the current times. I also believe that players' memories have been significantly influenced by nostalgia. I don't think there are many people who have been continually playing 'FF7' for the past twenty years, so the memories of the past have probably changed slightly in each player's mind. Additionally, 'FF7' has several spin-off works, and there are instances where scenes in these works differ from the original. Therefore, due to the passage of time and the existence of these spin-offs, there are subtle "distortions in perception" in players' memories. If you were to replay it now, you might think, "Wait, was this scene like this? I remembered it differently." This is true for me as well, and especially for Nojima-san, the scenario writer, who was concerned about these "distortions in perception." We aim to bring everything together into a unified whole. **Q: I have certainly felt the "distortion of perception" with the spin-offs. How is this "distortion" expressed in the game?** A: In the latter part of the game, there’s a scene in a white space where Sephiroth is present and Cloud is flying, and various visions can be seen. Among those visions, there is undoubtedly a version of the 'FF7' world that exists in the player's mind. They all represent 'FF7,' but each one is subtly different. It’s as if multiple alternate timelines exist; for example, 'In World A, this person is alive, but in World B, they are not.' These changes are made clear, but each person interprets them differently, memories may shift over time, and there may be discrepancies from the spin-offs. In this game, players experienced several worlds on different layers, and those visions express that concept. **Q: In Rebirth, the world map has made an appearance. Has Mr. Nomura's ideal world map finally become a reality?** A: Yes, this is truly thanks to the hard work on the ground. I believe we’ve been able to present the world map of 'FF7' that everyone, including us, has dreamed of. **Q: Indeed, there are plenty of mini-games and exploration elements. Is this because you want players to thoroughly explore the vast world map?** A: That's right. Without a purpose, there’s little motivation to explore every corner; it just becomes wandering in a large space. If that happens, the significance of creating a vast world map is lost. We’ve packed various elements in such a way that exploration leads to discoveries and rewards. [Source](
